source_text:
Γνοὺς ὑμῶν τὸ πολυεύτακτον τῆς κατὰ θεὸν ἀγάπης, ἀγαλλιώμενος προειλόμην ἐν πίστει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ προσλαλῆσαι ὑμῖν.
καταξιωθεὶς γὰρ ὀνόματος θεοπρεπεστάτου, ἐν οἷς περιφέρω δεσμοῖς ᾅδω τὰς ἐκκλησίας, ἐν αἷς ἕνωσιν: εὔχομαι σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ διὰ παντὸς ἡμῶν ζῆν, πίστεώς τε καὶ ἀγάπης, ἡς οὐδὲν προκέκριται, τὸ δὲ κυριώτερον Ἰησοῦ καὶ πατρός: ἐν ᾧ ὑπομένοντες τὴν πᾶσαν ἐπήρειαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ διαφυγόντες θεοῦ τευξόμεθα.
thought_title: Rejoicing in the Magnesians' ordered love and hoping in Christ
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, opens his letter to the church in Magnesia by praising their ordered love and stating his hope in Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Having known your well-ordered character of the love according to God, rejoicing I chose in faith of Jesus Christ to speak to you. For having been deemed worthy of a name most befitting God, in the bonds which I carry around I sing the churches, in which I pray for union of flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, who is our life through all things, and of faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and what is more authoritative, of Jesus and the Father; in whom enduring the whole assault of the ruler of this age and escaping, we will attain God.

choices.why: The adjective describes the Magnesians' love as marked by good order, matching Ignatius's emphasis on church order under the bishop.

choices.english: having been deemed worthy of a name most befitting God
choices.why: The passive participle keeps the sense that Ignatius received this worthiness from God, and 'most befitting God' renders the superlative literally.
rejected: being counted worthy of a most godly name
having been honored with a most divine name

choices.why: The verb is literal 'I sing' with the churches as direct object, preserving the poetic image of Ignatius celebrating the churches while in chains.

choices.english: who is our life through all things
choices.why: The genitive article with infinitive is rendered as a relative clause describing Christ as the source of life in every circumstance, keeping the literal force of 'through all things.'
rejected: through whom we live in all things

choices.why: The comparative of κύριος is rendered 'more authoritative' to preserve the sense of greater lordship or supremacy, not merely 'more important.'
The future middle of τυγχάνω with genitive means 'to obtain, attain,' and 'attain God' keeps the literal object without smoothing into 'reach God' or 'obtain God's presence.'

pass_b_english: I have come to know how well ordered your love for God is, and I rejoice greatly. So I have chosen to speak to you in the faith of Jesus Christ.

For I have been deemed worthy of a name most befitting God, and in the chains I carry around I sing to the churches, in which there is unity. I pray for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, who is our life through all things, and for faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and for what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. If we endure in him every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.

problems.quote: If we endure in him every assault
problems.source_quote: ἐν ᾧ ὑπομένοντες τὴν πᾶσαν ἐπήρειαν
problems.why: The relative pronoun ἐν ᾧ ('in whom') refers back to Jesus and the Father; English 'in him' drops the Father and obscures the antecedent.
problems.fix: in whom if we endure every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.
problems.ruling: Greek ‘ἐν ᾧ’ refers to both Jesus and the Father; English singular ‘him’ omits the Father, altering the referent.

edits.old: If we endure in him every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.
edits.new: If we endure in whom every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.

problems.why: Greek says “I sing to the churches,” not “sing the churches.” Agency and object are wrong.

problems.quote: the unity of faith and love
problems.why: Greek mentions “faith and love,” not “the unity of faith and love.”

problems.quote: praying that they may have the unity of the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ
problems.source_quote: εὔχομαι σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
problems.why: Greek asks for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, not their “unity.”
problems.fix: praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ
problems.ruling: Greek εὔχομαι σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος lacks 'unity'; translator added ἕνωσιν concept not present in that clause.

problems.quote: If we endure in whom every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.
problems.source_quote: ἐν ᾧ ὑπομένουσάς τὴν πᾶσαν ἐπήρειαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ διαφυγόντες θεοῦ τευξόμεθα
problems.why: Greek says “in whom, enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and having escaped, we will be saved by God,” not a conditional “if we endure… we will attain God.”
problems.fix: In whom, enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and having escaped, we will be saved by God.
problems.ruling: Greek ἐν ᾧ ὑπομένοντες...καὶ διαφυγόντες are participles, not conditional; θεοῦ τευξόμεθα means 'attain God,' not 'saved by God.'

edits.old: praying that they may have the unity of the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ
edits.new: praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ

edits.old: and the unity of faith and love
If we endure in whom every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.
edits.new: In whom, enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and having escaped, we will be saved by God.

fixed: All four confirmed problems were real and have been corrected.

problems.quote: praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, who is our life through all things, and faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father.
problems.why: The Greek includes a clause stating that the churches have unity, which is omitted in the English rendering.
problems.fix: …in which the churches have unity, praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, who is our life through all things, and faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father.

edits.old: I sing to the churches, praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ
edits.new: I sing to the churches, in which there is unity, praying for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ

problems.quote: and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. In whom, enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and having escaped, we will be saved by God.
problems.why: The sentence structure breaks down; 'In whom' starts a new sentence with an unclear antecedent, and the grammar is tangled.
problems.fix: Restructure: '...Jesus and the Father, who are supreme. By enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and escaping, we will be saved by God.'

edits.old: and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. In whom, enduring all assaults of the ruler of this age and having escaped, we will be saved by God.
edits.new: and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. If we endure in him every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.

fixed: The sentence structure was tangled; restructured the final clause to make the antecedent of 'in whom' clear and to render 'θεοῦ τευξόμεθα' as 'attain God' rather than 'be saved by God'.

polish.changed: Clarified the sentence structure and pronoun references, making the flow more natural for modern readers while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. In whom, enduring all assaults
notes.why: Sentence fragment; 'In whom' has no clear grammatical subject.
notes.fix: Reconstruct: 'in whom we endure all assaults of the ruler of this age.'

polish.changed: Clarified the tangled syntax by separating the prayer into distinct objects: the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, faith and love, and Jesus and the Father. Added 'for' before each object to make the prayer's content clear, and kept every claim and qualification intact.

notes.quote: faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father
notes.why: Syntax is tangled; meaning is unclear.
notes.fix: Restructure: 'faith and love, than which nothing is preferred; and more authoritative still, Jesus and the Father.'

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by separating the two ideas into distinct sentences, making the flow more natural for modern readers while preserving every claim and qualification exactly.

notes.quote: deemed worthy of a name most befitting God
notes.why: What 'name' means here is unclear; likely his title 'God-Bearer' but not obvious.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'name' refers to his title God-Bearer or his Christian calling.

dismissed.quote: how well ordered your love for God
dismissed.why: Greek says ‘abundant love for God’, not ‘well ordered love’
dismissed.note: πολυεύτακτον means 'very well ordered', so the English is correct.
